speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start with your current medication list; are you taking any antipsychotics or mood stabilizers? Also, when did you first notice these new involuntary movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: I'm glad your psychiatric symptoms are improving, but I need to focus on the new movements. Are these involuntary movements affecting your face, such as grimacing or lip-smacking, or do they involve your limbs and neck? Also, have you noticed any stiffness, tremors, or difficulty moving your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms sound very much like akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Have you noticed any muscle stiffness, twitching of the eyes, or a feeling that your limbs are being pulled? Also, have you recently changed your dose or missed any doses of your medication?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia secondary to Risperidone therapy.

To confirm this and assess severity, I need to know if these movements have been present since starting the medication and whether you have experienced any difficulty concentrating or sleeping due to the restlessness. REQUEST TEST: Akathisia_Agitation_Scale. REQUEST IMAGES: None required at this time.
